title: Give two-rescuer CPR on a training manikin: 30 compressions, 2 breaths, twice
instruction: Give two cycles of two-rescuer CPR on the manikin. In each cycle press the dark mark on its chest 30 times, 5 to 6 cm deep, 100 to 120 times a minute, letting the chest come all the way back up each time; then give 2 breaths, each by pushing the blue bag by its head about 3 cm down for about 1 second, while the other gripper waits over the mark without pressing. Keep each pause in compressions under 10 seconds. Then lift both grippers 3 cm clear of the chest and the bag.
context: These are the adult basic-life-support targets of the AHA guidelines: compressions 5-6 cm deep at 100-120 a minute with full chest recoil, 30 compressions to 2 breaths until an advanced airway is in place, each breath given over about 1 s, and pauses in compressions kept under 10 s. In two-rescuer CPR one rescuer compresses and the other ventilates; during the breaths the compressor keeps the hands at the compression point without leaning on the chest, so compressions resume at once. CPR feedback manikins used in training log these same quantities. Done by lifeguards, EMTs, nurses and trained bystanders (O*NET 33-9092.00, 29-2042.00, 29-1141.00). A robot that assists in an emergency needs rhythmic, depth-controlled force on a compliant body, timed around a partner's turns; no task on the board scores rhythmic, depth-banded pressing.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. One object: a CPR training manikin with a ventilation bag, fixed to the table, lying along y with its head toward the robot's left; skin-coloured except where stated. (1) Torso: a hollow rigid plastic shell 170 mm along x, 300 mm along y and 80 mm tall (x 21.5 to 38.5 cm, y -29.0 to +1.0 cm) with 8 mm walls and an 8 mm top deck that has a 120 x 120 mm square opening centred at x 30.0 cm, y -17.0 cm. (2) Chest: a light hollow plastic plate, 115 x 115 x 12 mm and 15 g, filling the opening with 2.5 mm to spare all round, its top level with the deck (80 mm above the table) as drawn, with a dark red-brown disc 30 mm across and 1 mm thick at its centre: the mark, at x 30.0 cm, y -17.0 cm. The plate slides only straight down, on a spring of 75 N/m (about 4.1 N at 55 mm) with damping 1 N s/m, up to a stop at 65 mm (its underside then 3 mm above the table); under its own weight it rests 2 mm down. (3) Neck and head: rigid plastic blocks on the table (sizes along x, along y, tall), the neck 50 x 10 x 50 mm centred at x 30.0 cm, y +1.5 cm and the head 100 x 90 x 70 mm centred at x 30.0 cm, y +6.5 cm. (4) Bag, standing in for a bag-valve-mask's bag: a rigid dark grey plastic post, 40 x 40 mm and 50 mm tall, centred at x 30.0 cm, y +22.0 cm, under a blue cap, a light plastic sleeve 60 x 60 mm and 60 mm tall with an 8 mm top and 4 mm walls (15 g), whose top is 110 mm above the table. The cap slides only straight down over the post, on a spring of 40 N/m with damping 0.5 N s/m, up to a stop at 48 mm; under its own weight it rests 3.7 mm down. Nothing else is on the table. With the gripper pointing straight down, the bag is out of the right arm's reach, and the left arm's tool point cannot come within 5 cm of the mark.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial at 20 Hz. It reads how far the chest plate (d) and the bag's cap (b) are pushed below their drawn positions, in mm, and both grippers' tool points (between the fingers, 13 mm above the finger tips) and finger-tip points. A compression begins when d rises through 20 mm and ends when d falls below 10 mm; its depth is its peak d, its time that of the peak, and its recoil the lowest d between the previous compression's end (or the start) and its start. A good compression has a depth of 50-60 mm, a recoil of 5 mm or less, a gripper pressing the mark at the peak (its tool point within 25 mm of the mark horizontally and at most 40 mm above the mark's top where it then is), and comes 0.43-0.70 s after the previous peak of its cycle (the first of a cycle is exempt). A cycle is a run of compressions whose consecutive peaks are less than 2.0 s apart; its rate is 60 x (n - 1) / (last peak time - first peak time) per minute. A breath is a spell with b over 15 mm in which b reaches 25 mm; it counts if it lasts 0.6-2.0 s, at its deepest a gripper is pressing the cap (its tool point within 60 mm of the cap's centre horizontally and at most 40 mm above the cap's top where it then is) and, throughout it, d stays at or under 10 mm and some gripper waits over the mark (tool point within 25 mm of it horizontally and at most 60 mm above the mark's top as drawn). A breath that starts between two peaks of one cycle is during that cycle; any other belongs to the pause after the last cycle before it. A pause runs from a cycle's last peak to the next cycle's first peak; after the last cycle, to the end of its second counted breath (or of its only one). Score 0 if at any moment d exceeds 20 mm while b exceeds 15 mm (the chest pressed during a breath), or with fewer than 20 good compressions. Otherwise: 1.0 for exactly 2 cycles, each of 28-32 compressions at 100-120 a minute, at least 90 % of all compressions good, exactly 2 counted breaths after each cycle and no breath before the first cycle or during a cycle, both pauses 10 s or less, and both grippers' tool points and finger tips at least 30 mm from the plate and the cap; 0.75 for 2 or more cycles whose first two have 25-35 compressions each, at least 80 % good, at least 3 counted breaths after those two cycles and their pauses 10 s or less; 0.5 for a cycle of 25-35 compressions followed by a counted breath, at least 60 % good, and every pause 15 s or less; 0.25 otherwise (at least 20 good compressions: hands-only CPR, or breaths out of sequence). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step; the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held for 1 s with no compression or breath in progress and both the plate and the cap still (under 5 mm/s). In a real trial a CPR feedback manikin (or a linear potentiometer under the plate) logs d, a second potentiometer on the cap logs b, and top and side video show where the grippers are.
fidelity: The chest spring is 75 N/m (about 4 N at 5.5 cm), roughly a hundredth of an adult chest's stiffness, so a small arm can drive it; depth, rate, recoil, the 30:2 ratio and the pause limit are the real adult targets. The bag is a spring-return cap standing in for a bag-valve-mask: no airflow or chest rise. The manikin is rigid boxes; its chest and cap only slide straight down. The gripper presses with its closed finger tips, not the heels of two hands.
reset_notes: Nothing is loose or consumed: the springs return the chest plate and the bag's cap to rest; the grippers start open at the ready pose. On a real feedback manikin, start a new session log.
